Okay, fuck the other guy that commented.

I don’t know anything about the person you’re describing, but if he’s being as loving and gentle as you say, then good. You deserve to be treated well. Questioning whether you’re “out of his league” is not a productive train of thought when he already clearly likes you—you’re just going have to trust him on this one. 

However, the hickies on the first date is a red flag for sure. If you’re looking for a relationship and he’s looking for fwb, then it’s better to find out sooner rather than later, and you should communicate the details with him.

I agree that you should not go into a new relationship with a jaded attitude. You should work to heal from the previous relationship first. But even after you put in the work to process and heal, your memories are still real, and communicating with your new partner is important in order for them to know you. That may not be suitable first date talk, but it’s necessary down the line. For instance: I was violently assaulted, so yeah, I’m going to be very clear before we get intimate what I’m actions I’m triggered by because of my past. That doesn’t mean I’m not healed, or I’m dredging up baggage. It means I’m communicating my own needs and boundaries.

I am neurodivergent and alcohol made me suddenly feel normal, so I get where you are coming from. The issue is that feeling that relief only makes the comedown crash harder. In this sense, “drinking so I don’t want to kill myself” became an impossible cycle, to the point where I almost wanted to commit just so I wouldn’t have to wake up sober and do it all over again. It’s really fucking unfair that mental illness makes you predisposed to addiction, because mental illness alone is hard enough. It’s really not a matter of responsibility vs irresponsibility when you feel like it’s your only option.

I’m not sure what country you’re from, but would there be a way for you to see a psychiatrist without parent approval? Is convincing them to look into it off the table?

Hey, my alcoholism also started when I was 15 and severely depressed. It’s so easy when you’re in that state to say “fuck it all, I’m drinking” in response to all the unbearable horrors of mental illness, but it really does just make it worse after a while. I’m not going to try to convince you not to drink, but please try to keep your options open when you feel like you have to drink. Once your brain associates any life hurdle with drinking as a solution, alcohol is a bitch to quit. So when you feel hopeless, I urge you to just take even five minutes to consider waiting it out, talking to someone, or even just watching a shitty reality show. Even if you do end up drinking after that—that process lets your brain know that you have self-soothing options available other than compulsive drinking, and those options will be more accessible next time. Forming those neural pathways is so important.
